samples.summary: Flipping the enforcement default to "enforce" denies viewer-role share links at attach, because AttachDocument always carries verb `rw`
samples.evidence: `isYorkieAuthEnforced()` returns true for unset, so any deployment that registers the webhook methods and configures nothing else now honors denials. But this repo's own integration test documents the verb behaviour it collides with: packages/backend/test/revision-history.e2e-spec.ts:371-383 — "Deliberately omits `AttachDocument` from the registered set. Empirically … `AttachDocument` always carries verb 'rw' — even for a brand-new local `Document` object with zero local changes … Gating it as the backend README's own walkthrough suggests would deny a viewer's very first attach outright". The documented registration walkthrough (packages/backend/README.md:211, packages/documentation/developers/self-hosting.md:573, docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:201) *does* add `AttachDocument`. In `decide()` → `checkAttribute()` (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:257) `verb === 'rw'` ⇒ `needWrite`, and `hasAccess()` line 293 returns `link.role === 'editor'`, so a viewer share link gets 403 on its first attach and the shared document never opens. The same hazard reaches `PushPull`: Yorkie derives the verb from `pack.HasChanges()`, and every mount pushes a change pack containing its `initialPresence` (shared-document.tsx:993 sets presence for the note mount; docs/slides/sheets/board mounts likewise), so a viewer's PushPull can also be classified `rw`. docs/design/yorkie-auth-webhook.md:270-283 states this exact risk is *unconfirmed* and that the mitigation is "the rollout must confirm viewer-link attach/PushPull requests actually carry verb `r` (watch the shadow logs) before flipping … =true" — this change removes that staged confirmation by making enforce the default while leaving the verb question open and the README's method list unchanged.

samples.summary: Share-link image upload failures are silently swallowed: the docs uploader rejects, but the notes engine only console.errors it
samples.evidence: `uploadImage = shareTokenImageUploader(token)` is a `DocsImageUpload` that *throws* on any failure (image-insert.ts:40-49 — `postShareTokenImage` rejects and nothing catches). The notes `UploadImage` contract (packages/notes/src/view/image-upload.ts:17-26) expects `null` for "host already reported the failure"; a rejection is caught in `beginUpload`'s `failed()` and only logged to the console, so an editor-role visitor whose upload 403s/500s sees the placeholder vanish with no error at all. The workspace route deliberately wraps the same call to toast (notes-detail.tsx:208-231, `return null` on every failure); this new mounting route does not.

samples.summary: An empty-string `YORKIE_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN` is passed straight to `jwt.sign`, throwing inside the auth-token injector
samples.evidence: `expiresIn: string = process.env.YORKIE_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN ?? '10m'` — `??` does not cover `''`, and the same pattern is repeated in yorkie.service.ts:48-52 (`configService.get('YORKIE_TOKEN_EXPIRES_IN') ?? '10m'`). With the variable present but empty, `jsonwebtoken` throws (`"expiresIn" should be a number of seconds or string representing a timespan`) from inside the injector, i.e. on every server-side attach / every script attach, as a rejected promise from the SDK's token refresh rather than at boot. Guarding with a truthiness check (or reusing AuthService's validated value) would fail loudly at construction instead.

samples.summary: Proxy traps break invariants if the wrapped store is ever non-extensible (frozen/sealed)
samples.evidence: `getPrototypeOf: () => null`, `isExtensible: () => true`, and `getOwnPropertyDescriptor`/`ownKeys` hiding configurable own props are all legal only while the *target* is extensible. If a caller (a test helper, a defensive `Object.freeze(store)`) hands in a frozen store, `Object.getPrototypeOf(view)`, `Object.isExtensible(view)`, `Object.keys(view)` and a plain spread all throw `TypeError` instead of returning a read-only view — the wrapper turns a read-only mount into a crash rather than a no-op. No such caller exists today, so the reach is contained, but the traps assume an invariant nothing enforces.

samples.summary: `canUndo`/`canRedo` forward to the real store while `undo`/`redo` are neutered, so the guarded handle can report a revertible edit it will refuse to revert
samples.evidence: `NOTE_STORE_READERS` includes `canUndo`/`canRedo` (bound to the raw target) while `HISTORY_METHODS` makes `undo`/`redo` return `null`. Any host reading `canUndo()` off the wrapped handle (rather than through `NoteEditorAPI`, which adds its own `!readOnly &&` at view/editor.ts:674) would enable a control that does nothing. Only masked today because `initialize` guards separately and `MemNoteStore` has no history in the tests.

samples.summary: Divider drag divides by a track width that can be 0
samples.evidence: `const track = rect.width - divider.offsetWidth;` then `const ratio = (ev.clientX - rect.left) / track;`. If the container is as narrow as the divider (or measures 0, e.g. a hidden/zero-size mount), `track` is 0 or negative: `0/0` yields `NaN`, and `Math.max(0.15, Math.min(0.85, NaN))` is `NaN`, so `flex: 1 1 NaN%` is written and the panes stop tracking the pointer until the next valid move. The old code divided by `rect.width`, which is only 0 in the degenerate case.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding checks out in the repository. isYorkieAuthEnforced (yorkie-auth-enforcement.ts:20-21) makes enforce the default when the variable is unset. checkAttribute (yorkie-auth.controller.ts:257) maps verb 'rw' to needWrite, and hasAccess (:293) grants write to share links only when role === 'editor', producing a 403 'no access to document' (:259-261). Only DetachDocument is exempt (:66, :196-198); AttachDocument is not special-cased anywhere, so no guard makes this unreachable. The repo's own e2e test (revision-history.e2e-spec.ts:371-383) documents empirically that AttachDocument always carries verb 'rw' even with zero local changes, and that gating it "would deny a viewer's very first attach outright" - which is why that test deliberately omits it from the registered method set. Yet the shipped registration walkthroughs do register AttachDocument (backend/README.md:211, self-hosting.md:573, yorkie-auth-webhook.md:201). The viewer path is reachable in normal use: shared-document.tsx:705,959 inject the share token and :975-1021 attach with initialPresence. The design doc is self-contradictory on this exact point: :221-223 says unset goes straight to enforce, while the risk section :270-283 still says the rollout must first confirm viewer requests carry verb 'r' via shadow logs before enforcing. Net effect for a deployment following this repo's documented setup with default config: a viewer share link is denied at its first attach and the shared document never opens - a broken core flow, critical under the correctness rubric. No named refutation ground applies (code is present as described, unguarded, and reachable).
